answer.rationale: The competitor's price cut directly targets price-sensitive SMB accounts, but exp_73 shows that acquisition via deep discounting produces a cohort with -12% 30-day retention and fails to survive renewal. Matching that strategy would accelerate churn and erode sustainable revenue. Instead, leverage what we know works: memory_44 confirms enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows with higher pipeline quality; memory_86 shows shortened onboarding lifts adoption; memory_91 confirms activation messaging drives week-one engagement. The optimal response is to deploy enterprise_sales_assist—shifting focus and resources toward higher-ACV, lower-churn enterprise accounts where we have proven conversion superiority, while using improved onboarding (memory_86) and in-product activation (memory_91) to stabilize the self-serve base without discounting. This preserves our pricing power, targets segments with better unit economics and retention, and avoids the trap of competing on price where we lose money on renewal. A standard_experiment scale allows measured rollout of sales resources to enterprise prospect segments while monitoring SMB churn independently.
